Sure! Those coordinates point to the Googleplex in Mountain View, California.

| Latitude | Longitude |
|----------|-----------|
| 37.4224764 | –122.0842499 |

If you reverse‑geocode them with the Google Geocoding API (or any other reverse‑geocoding service), you’ll get an address similar to:

```
1600 Amphitheatre Parkway
Mountain View, CA 94043
United States
```

So the latitude and longitude you supplied are already the exact coordinates for that address. If you need to confirm or retrieve additional details (e.g., formatted address, place ID, etc.), you can call the Geocoding API with a request like:

```
https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=YOUR_API_KEY
```

The response will include the full address, place ID, and other metadata.
